title: Upper surface friction
description: Essential: Student states that the frictional force on the upper surface of block B is 0 N, recognizing no relative motion between blocks.

title: Lower surface friction
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates the frictional force on the lower surface of B as 16 N, applying equilibrium for uniform motion.

title: Friction coefficient calculation
description: Essential: Student calculates the coefficient of kinetic friction as 0.2 using the correct normal force for the combined system.

title: Equilibrium reasoning
description: Important: Student applies Newton's first law to analyze forces on either individual blocks or the combined system during uniform motion.

title: Normal force identification
description: Important: Student correctly identifies the normal force as supporting the combined weight of both blocks (80 N total).

title: Incorrect normal force
description: Pitfall: Student uses only one block's weight (40 N) instead of the combined weight (80 N) when calculating the friction coefficient.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Student assigns incorrect sign or direction to friction forces, or confuses static/kinetic friction concepts.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student maintains consistent units throughout calculations and includes units with final answers.
